title: Graded Degradation Inspector and Circuit Safeguard
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: Requests routed to certain regions or tiers sometimes experience short-lived overloads (429s), backend model timeouts, or elevated error rates. Without a unified detection and graded response, we either do nothing until user impact is high or take blunt fallbacks that cause quality regressions and cost spikes.

Goal: Implement an inspector + circuit safeguard that automatically detects overload/error/timeouts, computes a per-(region,tier,model_variant,tenant) trip score, and triggers graduated mitigations: probe-based canary to half-open, targeted model-variant fallbacks, temporary routing throttles, or full circuit open for aggressive isolation. Must integrate with routing policies, Dedicated/Dedicated burst, and per-tenant isolation rules.
proposed_solution:
Design components:
1) Graded Degradation Inspector (GDI): sliding-window signal aggregator that consumes 429 rates, p95+p99 latency, timeout counts, and 5xx/error rates. Uses an exponential-decay scoring function to compute trip_score per key (region|tier|model_variant|tenant). Configurable weights for each signal.
2) Circuit Safeguard Controller (CSC): policy engine that maps trip_score -> action bands (monitoring, soft-degrade, probe-half-open, open-circuit). Actions include: route to fallback model variant, apply per-route throttling, redirect to Dedicated pool, or open circuit for >X minutes.
3) Recovery Probes: periodic lightweight probes to assess health when in half-open or open with probation. Probes can be synthetic requests or realtime-sampled traffic.
4) Integration: CSC exposes a stable API consumed by router to enact per-request routing decisions, and by Console for visibility and manual overrides.

Algorithm highlights:
- Signals window: 60s, 5m, 15m buckets aggregated with EMA (alpha tunable).
- Trip score computation: weighted sum normalized to 0..100. Example default weights: 429_rate(0.35), p95_latency(0.25), timeout_count(0.25), error_rate(0.15).
- Action bands: 0-20 (ok), 21-45 (soft-degrade: route small % to fallback variant), 46-70 (probe-half-open + escalate throttles), 71-100 (open circuit + isolate region-tier for N minutes).
- Hysteresis: require trip_score persist above threshold for M consecutive windows before action; require decay below lower threshold for K windows before recovery to avoid flip-flapping.
- Tenant probation & decay: per-tenant decay multiplier to avoid long tail punishing small tenants.
- Cost / quality guardrails: fallback policy must respect per-tenant quality budgets (max % fallback) and cost budgets (don't route >X qps to costlier Dedicated path without approval).
metrics_and_telemetry: Alert: sustained trip_score > 70 for 3 windows -> paging on-call
Trace: attach routing_decision_id to request traces for debugging fallbacks
acceptance_criteria: GDI computes trip_score for synthetic traffic and matches expected score for controlled signal injection tests
CSC takes the configured action band after hysteresis thresholds are met in integration tests
Router applies fallback model variant for at least 1% traffic in soft-degrade and respects tenant fallback budget
Recovery probes transition circuit from open -> half_open -> closed after healthy responses verified
Console dashboard shows trip_score/time series and allows manual open/close of a circuit
Load test: under a simulated 30% regional capacity drop, overall global error rate increases < 2% and affected tenants see graceful degradation per policy
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (feature flag off): unit + e2e tests + local simulator
Phase 1 (internal demo): enable for internal tenants in us-west, verbose logging, dry-run mode where CSC only emits events but does not actuate
Phase 2 (canary): enable soft-degrade actuation for 3% of traffic in us-west and eu-central, monitor metrics for 48h
Phase 3 (regional expansion): add more regions and enable probe-based recovery, enable tenant probation rules for multi-tenant workloads
Phase 4 (global): flip feature flag for all regions with graduated thresholds released via runtime-1.22
testing_plan: Unit tests: scoring function edge cases, EMA behavior, hysteresis windows
Integration: simulate 429 spikes, increased p95, and timeouts across region/tier combinations; assert CSC actions
Chaos test: kill model instances to simulate partial outage and validate circuit opens and recovers without cascading failures
Performance: ensure GDI + CSC adds <2ms median overhead to routing decision path under 10k rps
Security: verify actions cannot be triggered by malformed signals (validate signal integrity)
implementation_notes: Prefer streaming aggregation in router proxies (Envoy filter) for 60s window then backfill to central aggregator for 5m/15m EMAs
Store per-key state in sharded Redis with TTL tied to hysteresis windows; use optimistic concurrency on state transitions
Expose policy config via Console and runtime-config service so thresholds can be tuned without deploys
Fallback model mapping: keep prioritized list of compatible variants with metadata (cost_index, quality_index) so CSC can pick the least-quality-regressive option within budget
Add telemetry tag 'fallback_budget_exceeded' when a tenant hits fallback cap to avoid silent broad-spectrum routing changes
risks_mitigation: Risk: cascading fallbacks push traffic to Dedicated pools causing cost spike. Mitigation: per-tenant cost budget and global emergency cutoff flag that forces safe slow degrade instead of Dedicated fallback
Risk: oscillation between open/closed. Mitigation: strict hysteresis and exponential backoff on probe frequency after repeated flips
Risk: misconfigured weights cause false positives. Mitigation: default conservative weights + staged canary + config validation linting
Risk: attackers craft traffic to trigger fallbacks for competitor tenants. Mitigation: apply tenant-level signal smoothing, require minimum qps before circuits can open for tenant-specific keys
open_questions: Should probe requests be routed to the same model variant or always to the highest-stability variant? Tradeoffs: signal fidelity vs conservative false negatives.
What is the default decay half-life for EMA across 60s/5m/15m windows? Ops prefers faster reactions for short spikes (alpha=0.6) but Product wants stability (alpha=0.2).
How to prioritize fallback candidates between cheaper quantized variants and smaller safer models when both are available?
What SLAs permit automated open-circuit for enterprise customers and what exceptions must be opt-out?

2026-03-04 Avery Chen: Implemented local simulator for synthetic 429/timeouts to validate trip_score dynamics. Observed flip-flapping with naive thresholds; added hysteresis proposal.
2026-03-06 Product review (Lena Morales): Request to add per-customer fallback budget and a human-notify threshold before Dedicated fallback kicks in. Marked for Phase 2 gating.
2026-03-08 Reliability review (Diego Alvarez): Suggested probe backoff exponent of 2.5 after three failed probe rounds. Also asked for explicit metrics before and after route actuation.
2026-03-10 Engineering note: Chose Redis sharded state store for speed; follow-up task to evaluate placement in metadata service for cross-region consistency.
2026-03-12 Ops: Load test scheduled 2026-03-20 to validate <2ms added latency at 10k rps. Need infra approval for canary traffic to eu-central.
2026-03-14 Avery Chen: RFC branch opened and initial unit tests passing. Next: infra PR for Envoy filter integration and run the canary in us-west dry-run mode.
